<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/embedder-openai`, `@objectstack/knowledge-memory`, `@objectstack/service-knowledge`, `@objectstack/service-settings`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **85** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **9** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/ai.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx`  _(via maxTokens (symbol, a field of interface Bounds; a field of interface ResolvedSplit))_
- `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx`  _(via IEmbedder (symbol, a top-level interface), KnowledgeService (symbol, a top-level class), KnowledgeServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class), OpenAIEmbedder (symbol, a top-level class), maxChars (symbol, a field of interface Bounds; a field of interface ResolvedSplit), maxInputTokens (symbol, a field of class OpenAIEmbedder; a field of interface AdapterEmbeddingDescriptor; a field of interface IEmbedder; a field of interface ResolveSplitInput; a field of interface ServiceSetup), sourceId (symbol, a const object of class KnowledgeMemoryAdapter))_
- `content/docs/api/data-api.mdx`  _(via sourceId (symbol, a const object of class KnowledgeMemoryAdapter))_
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via sourceId (symbol, a const object of class KnowledgeMemoryAdapter))_
- `content/docs/getting-started/common-patterns.mdx`  _(via maxTokens (symbol, a field of interface Bounds; a field of interface ResolvedSplit))_
- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/sharing-service.mdx`  _(via sourceId (symbol, a const object of class KnowledgeMemoryAdapter))_
- `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx`  _(via IEmbedder (symbol, a top-level interface), IKnowledgeAdapter (symbol, a top-level interface), KnowledgeDocumentSchema (symbol, a top-level const), KnowledgeReindexResult (symbol, a top-level interface), KnowledgeService (symbol, a top-level class), KnowledgeServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class), docHash (symbol, a field of interface ChunkRecord; a field of interface StoredDocument), indexDocument (symbol, a method of class KnowledgeService), listDocuments (symbol, a method of class KnowledgeMemoryAdapter), maxChars (symbol, a field of interface Bounds; a field of interface ResolvedSplit), maxInputTokens (symbol, a field of class OpenAIEmbedder; a field of interface AdapterEmbeddingDescriptor; a field of interface IEmbedder; a field of interface ResolveSplitInput; a field of interface ServiceSetup), minChars (symbol, a field of interface ResolvedSplit), reindexSource (symbol, a method of class KnowledgeService), runKnowledgeAdapterContract (symbol, a top-level function), sourceId (symbol, a const object of class KnowledgeMemoryAdapter), chunk_target (literal, a string literal in KnowledgeServicePlugin))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-0.mdx`  _(via sourceId (symbol, a const object of class KnowledgeMemoryAdapter))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via sourceId (symbol, a const object of class KnowledgeMemoryAdapter))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-6.mdx`  _(via sourceId (symbol, a const object of class KnowledgeMemoryAdapter))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **9** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/ai.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **26** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **178** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4ed453dc211f24114c36133cb016515f377d2d5c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a9947ebcda6f1ffccebcf1a22da3cc766dcab6e9` — the merge of head `c84c242aa76ac788c77052c6a33335912f58ee17` into base `4ed453dc211f24114c36133cb016515f377d2d5c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a9947ebcda6f1ffccebcf1a22da3cc766dcab6e9 && git checkout a9947ebcda6f1ffccebcf1a22da3cc766dcab6e9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4ed453dc211f24114c36133cb016515f377d2d5c c84c242aa76ac788c77052c6a33335912f58ee17 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4ed453dc211f24114c36133cb016515f377d2d5c && git merge --no-ff c84c242aa76ac788c77052c6a33335912f58ee17

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4ed453dc211f24114c36133cb016515f377d2d5c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4ed453dc211f24114c36133cb016515f377d2d5c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c84c242aa76ac788c77052c6a33335912f58ee17`
Local-runs: probe — three runs in a throwaway worktree at the head, each for a check the brief asked to be reproduced rather than read: (1) `build-migration-registry.ts`, to read the generated `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR[18]`; (2) the pin's three parse assertions against `knowledge-document.zod.ts`, at head and with the `retiredKey()` line deleted; (3) `splitter.ts` against its six golden files, hand-made edge cases and a 4,000-document property run. No vitest, no build, no dogfood. Worktree removed.
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/knowledge-document.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ai/knowledge-source.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/embedder.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/knowledge-adapter.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/knowledge-service.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/retired-keys/18.ai__KnowledgeChunk__metadata.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.knowledge-chunk-metadata-retired.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template + packages/spec/src/ai/knowledge-document.test.ts, packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json, packages/services/service-knowledge/src/split/splitter.ts, packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-service.ts, packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-service-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-knowledge/src/testing.ts, packages/plugins/knowledge-memory/src/index.ts, packages/plugins/embedder-openai/src/index.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/knowledge.manifest.ts, .changeset/37098-knowledge-splitter.md

Face: schema (`record-recognisers --template --paths` on the 62 changed paths returns the eight `packages/spec/src` files above as `hits`). Read outside the diff, not reviewed: `.claude/skills/spec-property-retirement/SKILL.md`, the `ActionDescriptor.isAsync` kit (protocol 17), `packages/spec/src/conversions/types.ts`, `packages/spec/src/shared/token-estimate.ts`, ADR-0161 K6 and K8, `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Deviation 1 holds: no D2 conversion and no `retiredAfter` is owed.** A conversion rewrites stored stack metadata, and `KnowledgeChunk` is in none:
  - `stack.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/conversions/**` and `packages/spec/src/kernel/**` name neither `KnowledgeDocument` nor `KnowledgeChunk`.
  - At the merge base no file under `packages/services`, `packages/plugins`, `apps`, `examples` or `ui/packages` names `KnowledgeChunk` or reads a document's `chunks`. The only `chunks` there is RAGFlow's own API response.
  - No adapter stores a chunk-level `metadata`: `knowledge-memory` stores the document's `metadata` beside each passage, and `knowledge-ragflow` sends whole documents.
  - ADR-0161 K6 reads the same way for the source: "No stored row carries any of them".
  - `retiredAfter` is declared only on `MetadataConversion` (`conversions/types.ts`), so with no conversion there is nowhere to write it. The seat's later wording ("`retiredAfter` the latest stable") assumed a conversion; the skill's §3 last item is the governing text: a key with no source to rewrite takes the D3 `semantic` entry alone.
  - The `17.action-descriptor-is-async-retired` kit is the same shape: a tombstone, a retired-key row, one D3 semantic entry, no conversion.
- **Deviation 2 holds: the major-18 registration is complete.**
  - Tombstone: `metadata: retiredKey(...)` on `KnowledgeChunkSchema`. The message follows the house form (the full key in backticks, "was removed in @objectstack/spec 18", why it was inert, "Delete the key.", the live mechanism). It carries no `os migrate meta` sentence, which is right with no conversion and matches the `isAsync` message.
  - Retired-key row: the entry file `retired-keys/18.ai__KnowledgeChunk__metadata.ts` exports `'ai/KnowledgeChunk:metadata'`. `registry.ts` is git-ignored and generated; run at the head, the generator writes that string inside the `18: [` block of `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR` (311 retired-key entries in all). Nothing is hand-typed.
  - D3: `semantic/18.knowledge-chunk-metadata-retired.ts` has non-empty `reason` and `acceptanceCriteria`, and the generator places it in `step18`. The `STEP18_RATIONALE` fragment has the same id, sits in id order before `list-view-filterable-fields-retired`, and takes `order: 125`, which no other fragment uses.
  - Authorable surface: `"ai/KnowledgeChunk:metadata [RETIRED]"` replaces the live line.
  - Pin: with the `retiredKey()` line deleted, both parse refusals in `knowledge-document.test.ts` fail ("did not throw") and the clean-parse case still passes; at head all three pass. The file was restored to blob `4fca15827da`. The `@ts-expect-error` case and build gate (b2) go red on the same deletion by reading; neither was run.
- **Additive members.** `IEmbedder.maxInputTokens?`, `IKnowledgeAdapter.capabilities?` and `embedding?`, `AdapterCapabilities.chunks?`, `KnowledgeReindexResult.failed?` and `failures?`, `KnowledgeDocument.chunks?`, `KnowledgeChunk.headingPath?` and `ObjectKnowledgeSource.split?` are all optional. An implementation written before this change still type-checks. The generated baselines add names and remove none.
- **`knowledge.chunk_overlap` has no reader left.** A case-insensitive search of the head for `chunk_overlap` and `chunkOverlap` finds the changeset, the root `CHANGELOG.md`, ADR-0161's readings table, and three comments or assertions in `service-settings`. The specifier is out of the manifest, all 11 translation packs carry zero mentions, and the manifest is at `version: 2`.
- **The splitter, as run.**
  - All six golden files reproduce byte for byte.
  - 4,000 seeded documents with bounds wider than the dev's (limits from 4 tokens, `maxChars` from 2, CRLF, tabs, emoji, the ideographic space, both strategies): no passage over `maxChars` or over the token budget, none empty, and `recursive` loses no text.
  - `whole` over the budget answers a failure with the estimate and the budget; it returns no passage. `whole` with no limit known checks nothing.
  - 「依照第3.2 条报销400.50 元。」 at `maxChars: 14` cuts into 「依照第3.2 条报销」 and 「400.50 元。」: neither decimal is cut.
- **The service splits once.** `prepareDocuments` is the only place `splitDocument` is called, and all three `adapter.upsert` sites (`indexDocument`, the reindex walk, `writeSynced`) go through it. An adapter without `capabilities.chunks` gets the documents untouched. The suite compares what the adapter received with `splitDocument`'s output by `toEqual`, and a hit with a passage by id and text.
- **`knowledge-memory` no longer splits.** `chunkAndEmbed` and `CHUNK_TARGET` are gone; `embedPassages` maps `doc.chunks` one to one. The organization filter from #37256 still runs before the metadata filter and the ranking.
- **Check-runs on the head:** 60 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed. `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and `Test Core` 1 to 10 are among the successes. The dogfood shards are among the skipped, as on every PR.
- **K = 8** against `main` `dfdebfadd58`, merge base `f9fda2a4f84` (the #37256 merge). `git merge-tree --write-tree` is clean (tree `a50f7e33ba1`), and none of main's eight commits touches a path of this diff.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/spec: minor` is right for `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`; the skill forbids `major` and the BREAKING banner carries the break. `Check Changeset` passes.
- `patch` on the four other packages matches how #37256 shipped the same kind of change.
- `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` is right: the diff adds `split` and narrows `KnowledgeChunk.metadata`, and narrowed wins.
- The BREAKING section names both removals, each with FROM, TO and a one-line fix. The `adr-0087: registered knowledge-chunk-metadata-retired` marker names an entry that exists. `knowledge.chunk_overlap` is a settings key with no spec registry, so the BREAKING entry is its whole disposition, as the seat ruled.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag, no D2 conversion and no `retiredAfter`: answered in ①, holds.
- Dev flag, two test pins outside the claim's file list (`settings-visibility-declaration.pin.test.ts` 90 to 87, `knowledge.manifest.test.ts`): both are tripwires on the manifest this card edits, and the new count follows from the diff (one specifier with a predicate removed, two predicates dropped).
- Dev flag, no `minChars` ≤ `maxChars` refinement: `resolveSplit` clamps `minChars` to `maxChars`, a test pins it, and the key's description says it.
- Dev flag, `docHash` does not cover the passages: true in the code (`chunks` is set after `computeDocHash`), and both doc pages and the changeset say so.
- Open question "which major": settled as major 18 by the seat; built that way.
- SQL push-down: no new id materialisation or in-app join. The reindex deletes the failed documents of one page by id through the adapter, which is the adapter contract's own door.
- S1 (should-fix) — the `Skills-docs:` line reads `none in this change`, and its own reason says `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` does not yet teach `split`. By the claim template that is `follow-up owed`, and the owed card exists: #37292. The line should read `Skills-docs: follow-up #37292`. This is the seat's rewrite of the PR body, not a dev fix, and it moves no head. #37292 should also cover `SKILL.md` lines 281 to 284, which say chunking is "NOT platform metadata": that sentence becomes false when this lands.

### ④ Design judgment

- **The narrowing takes away nothing an author had.** `KnowledgeChunk.metadata` had no producer and no reader on `main`, so a value written there was dropped. ADR-0161 K8 item 5 says #37098 "gives it one or removes it", and the seat chose removal. The schema now refuses what it used to drop in silence.
- **K8 item 5** is built as written: `chunks?` on the document, the reshaped `KnowledgeChunk` with `headingPath?`, `capabilities?: { chunks?: boolean }`, and whole documents for an adapter that declares nothing.
- **K8 item 6** is built in part, as the ADR assigns it: `embedding?: { maxInputTokens? }` only. `model`, `dimensions` and `variant` wait for item 8's PR. The service reads the descriptor in `prepareDocuments` on every batch and keeps no copy.
- **K8 item 10**: `split` sits on the object arm with `strategy`, `maxChars?` and `minChars?`, and the splitter reads all three.
- **Changeset and 维护者速读**: each sentence checked against the code is true, apart from N6.
- N1 — `markdown` can drop a heading that has no text under it. `# A` then `# B` with nothing else gives one passage, `B`. `## B` then `## C` at the end of a document gives `A > C` and loses `B`. A bodiless heading longer than half the bound is dropped whole. The no-loss property covers `recursive` only.
- N2 — The character-level cut does not look at punctuation: 「他说：“不行。”然后走了。」 at `maxChars: 12` is cut between `。` and `”`. The sentence rule itself holds, and this is the last level the card allows.
- N3 — `KnowledgeChunkSchema.parse` has no caller in the platform outside its test. The service builds chunks as typed objects, and `indexDocument` refuses any `chunks` before a parse could run. `tsc` is the channel that reaches an author; the parse refusal reaches only a consumer who parses.
- N4 — `KnowledgeSplitSchema` is a plain `z.object` (the strictness ledger's `ai/` count goes 112 to 113), and `registerSource` parses nothing. From untyped code a misspelt key is ignored and an unknown `strategy` string cuts as `recursive`, in silence. The source loader of ADR-0161 row 3 is where that closes.
